steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Down!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: In your dreams!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Fancy that, you can still struggle...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm not holding this one back, Dame Strollo!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You—read me?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who knew you could bite off more than you could chew?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Unripe. You're just relying on the Voice of Mundane... Your control of Arts is still in its infancy—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hrragh!!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Huff, *pant*, *pant*...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: D—Did that get her...?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Heh, I never thought you'd be one to best me, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So you admit defeat?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Hmph. A loss is a loss. What, does not admitting it make it my victory instead?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You... Why are you unperturbed?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Because... how exactly can you lay a finger on me?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'm the Lehnsfrau of this city. It's night, you broke into a concert hall I administrate, and you attempted to tear down legitimate renovations ratified by my own person.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You even injured me as I did my best to stop you—

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Graf Urtica, Rhodes Islander, and you, Czerny. You should be the worried ones, isn't that right?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: As despicable as ever, Gertrude.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Despicable? Is that how you treat your patron, your back of over a decade?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Czerny, I allowed you to use this concert hall.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You're no more than a mere Infected. Your position? I gave you that too.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Your cherished Afterglow could only limp its way to the present day on MY benevolence.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Don't forget that.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: How dare—!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: All of you, kindly leave.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I wouldn't be so sure.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Graf Urtica—this title carries with it disgrace, all throughout Leithanien.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But it also means that wherever I go, the Empresses' informants are sure to be.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: And what if they are? I told you, you're only making vain attempts to destroy my music hall.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Even if Their Majesties' agents were to show themselves, they would arrest you by all rights, not me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Biegler! Biegler!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You have to have witnessed this all now, right?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Do you still intend to fold your arms and watch?!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I saw the grand Graf Urtica fall to breaking and entering a concert hall, in the dead of night, with a gang. Aside from that, I saw nothing.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Did you not hear her plot?!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Do you mean Gräfin Strollo's plot, or the Graf Urtica's plot jointly schemed with her?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I did in fact hear.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: However, even if I recorded your entire dialogue just now, that doesn't prove a thing.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Evidence, Graf. Everything needs carefully selected evidence. What proves Gräfin Strollo intended to act against the Empresses?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Proof. You come to me at this moment and raise the matter of proof...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Right. The Voice of Mundane!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: We discovered there was research into the Voice of Mundane in the sewers!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Seems you're not off the ball after all, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: What research? I know nothing about this.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Feigning stupidity at this point's passé, Gräfin Strollo.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You may not be directly linked to the notes and plans in that sewer laboratory, but we have our ways.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: With our leads there, it'll be a walk in the park to find your other little bases.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: You are presently suspected of launching research into the Voice of Mundane forbidden under Their Majesties' decree. I want you to come with me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait, because she was researching the Voice and nothing else?!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Let me reiterate to you again, Graf Urtica, and the rest of you.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: As long as you have no clear evidence, proof your 'foul product' is going to blow up like you say it does—

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Every accusation you throw at her turns into slander, nothing else.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Let me take a look at those Voice of Mundane research files! I can give you exhaustive evidence!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Very sorry, but that's classified Leithanian information. I can't hand it over to a foreign organization.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're just wishing it out of existence!

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: There's a lot in these lands that doesn't go the way you want it, Fräulein.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But...!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let it go, Hibiscus.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He's made his point very clear. Our discoveries aren't enough to convict Gräfin Strollo.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And he only showed himself because he found other evidence to do so.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I should even be thanking you for deigning to show up in the wake of my hissy fit. Isn't that right, Biegler, my dear spy?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: I'll be honest, if I had to compare you and Gräfin Strollo as nobles, I'd say you win out in my books, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: And you, Herr Czerny.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: We have Gräfin Strollo contained now. Even if whatever your friends are worried about is real, either way, the concert's safe.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Of course, I still recommend you cancel it. Safest for settling this.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I thought the concert tomorrow had already been forbidden.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Whether you hold it remains up to you.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Okay, Gräfin Strollo, I believe your loyalty to the Empresses. I'd just like to take you for... breakfast. You wouldn't refuse my invitation, would you?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Hah. Breakfast in these early hours? Very well.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Graf Urtica, you will regret betraying me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll regret many a thing, but that is the one matter I never will.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Well, we've just let them go.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Gertrude...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You still had a word waiting for her?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If profanity counts for a word.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide still hasn't woken.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Leave him with me, I'll set off straight away and bring him to the Rhodes Island landship.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're taking him away?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I am. He'll only get the proper treatment at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I won't allow it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Even if you can pacify his condition, what will you do about the Voice of Mundane?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't doubt your medical prowess, but is that something you can truly solve?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I can't promise.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But we've got no other choice now.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't tell me you still hope Gertrude'll help you get rid of it through ensemble?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I can only hope.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How long will it take from Vyseheim to your landship, I ask you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You won't say. Because you know Kreide isn't likely to make it there.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But even if what Gertrude says is true, are you really going to sacrifice yourself to do this?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: As long as I can do it, why shouldn't I?
Hibiscus stares, blank, for a spell.
The look in his eyes now, compared to when she first met this young man—the difference is like black and white.
He's serious, she thinks.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Even if I help you to the best of my ability, we know too little about the Voice of Mundane, and what we do know was all told to us by the Countess. We're sifting through fact and fiction...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Looks like I made it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir, you...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: If you need more info about the Voice of Mundane, I have this project plan right here.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir, did you...?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You pulled the same thing as Biegler...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You probably imagined, but Kreide's a fin who slipped through the program's net back in the day.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: How could the Empresses let such a wildcard wander freely, you know?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But you've been roaming together for more than a decade!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: And that's why no one ever suspected it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But didn't Biegler say it was classified—

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Which is why I filched it from where he kept it.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: If I can save Kreide, then the hell does it matter if anyone's shown this damned plan?! And it's a long-overdue damning if you ask me!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: *cough* *cough*, *cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: C—Calm down, you're still very weak...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Let me see the plan papers, Hibiscus. You take this old fellow somewhere to rest.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir... does Kreide—does he know?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I never told him, but he's very smart. I'm sure he has a vague guess.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: This is too cruel to him.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Cruel.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Fräulein, do you know how I became an Infected?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Surely you've heard how in the age before the Empresses' rule, Leithanien had explored classical Originium Arts to heights hardly surpassable.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: So do you know the price Leithanien paid, to reach those heights?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Countless human sacrifices, among which were huge numbers of Infected.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Yes. Infected.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: During that period, some Kurfürsten were even handing over Infected to a regular quota, and they treated this as a custom.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But Infected are people too. It's not like they'd let their lives be thrown away.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: So, can you guess what happened in the end?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You don't mean...?!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: It looks like you have.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Just slash your arm with Originium, and now you qualify as an Infected too.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: That's how mine came about.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Melody... it's melody. The Voices of the Mundane are the melodies the Witch King left behind!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I can't believe this...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: No, this is the only way it makes sense!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: He wasn't just Leithanien's mightiest Caster. The Witch King was also Leithanien's most feared musician.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: His mastery of music was at the epitome. Some even said his insight into music was of the same grade as his Originium Arts research.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But rhythm, tonality, texture... he threw those raw elements that make up the beauty of music to the hounds. Every piece of his left in this world is filled with murder and devastation.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: His opuses have long been forbidden pieces in Leithanien. If the Voice of Mundane is a string of melodies left by the Witch King—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Then the Voice is without a doubt a remnant opus of his, and you are its very extents.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: We are not his opus!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You shouldn't deceive yourself. Moreover, if this is the case...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You have a solution?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I need you to perform the ensemble that repelled those Originium slugs again.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: When you did that, you grasped the Voices inside yourselves, didn't you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ensemble? Right now?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Do you comprehend the situation we're in here?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I do, and I know it better than you do!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But—!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Let's hear Herr Czerny out, Ebenholz.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide, are you alright? Did you come here alone?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Andante brought me over.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But you can't double the Voice of Mundane's melody again like you did before. It did something wrong to you last time...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I don't want to leave any regrets.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Alright... Herr Czerny, what did you think of?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If the Voice can be said to be a string of melodies, then whether those remnants who used you for their experiment, or Gertrude...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Their aim has to be to conduct the Originium Arts contained within that melody, or should I say, the melody that flows within this Originium Arts.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Which is to say, their exploration of the Voice is entirely to unearth the supposed secrets within.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: In plain words, they're trying to make the Voice more 'clear,' more 'beautiful.'

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thus, there is one thing I can very definitively tell you—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: There is no method that can 'transfer' the Voice anywhere in these plans.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm not surprised anymore.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But that's not because doing so would be too difficult. Precisely the opposite. It's because, in their eyes, it would be a waste of what they have.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Because every melody the Witch King left behind is different. Each comes from its own period, and contains its own completely separate emotions and ideas.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: What sense can there be in putting two entirely different songs together?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Just as when you performed together, the further you pursue it, the more disastrous the effects become.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Even the Originium slugs fled because they felt your performance to be far too ear-bleeding.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I presume they've done similar transfer experiments before, and realized how bad the results were... then.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: They did.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: However, even if two pieces are diametrically opposed, a sufficient lead-in can still be enough to accomplish the transition.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Therefore, I want you to perform my Morgen und Abend.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Upon which, I want you to dig your own selves out from within the piece, just as you did that evening.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I have to feel the melody the Voice of Mundane left within you, and then, I will write you a new song.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Wait. No matter what, you need something to hold the Voice so you can transfer it.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And the experiment results said all attempts to implant two Voices in one person failed.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll be the vessel, is that what you mean?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't trust that little determination you have to be enough for self-sacrifice, boy.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I will try with all my might, through performance, to drag the Voices from the both of you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If I cannot, I will personally serve as this receptacle, if I am able to.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why would you go so far for us?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If I remember correctly, my Morgen und Abend was your turning point in learning flute.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And so what?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: So it's likely you heard of how I came to write it. That Gertrude woman had to turn it into a blasted 'selling point' for me, though I never wanted for anyone else to know.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You lost your dearest, closest friend, and you wrote the piece in your grief.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: 'Grief.'

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That description was far off the mark.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You should be using the term 'indignation.'

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That was the first time I came to find that life would not unfold how I imagined it, and the first time I knew what music meant to me—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: My rebellion against a fixed fate.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Turning ordinary civilians into Infected... That's too cruel...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I have no idea how many times I cursed the Witch King in those days, but perhaps someone heard my tirades.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: However, before they could send me to the laboratories, Their Majesties had overthrown the Witch King. I was saved.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: And that's why I swore to dedicate the rest of my life to Their Majesties' cause.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: And so you became a spy?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I can't tell you what I did when I was an agent, and you don't need to know.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: All you need to know is that I was the agent who found the Witch King's Remains that had been researching the Voice of Mundane.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: By the time we found them, they had already experimented on Kreide and failed. It's why his body is the way it is now.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You didn't plan to save him, right?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: How'd you know?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: From what I know, when the Twin Empresses ascended to the throne, they issued an edict that forbade all Witch King era research, and the Voice of Mundane research obviously fell into that category.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But if the Voice of Mundane is really that amazing, I can't imagine that not a single person has turned his attention to it in the twenty years since the Witch King was overthrown.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: What's more... 'The Witch King left his mark within.' 'The Witch King weaved his power into the melody.' The Witch King himself is the core of these ideas.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Deep down, their pursuit of the Voice of Mundane might actually be nothing more than worshipping the Witch King himself.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: And given the way that Mr. Biegler does things, I'd say a spy's principles lie with serving the Twin Empresses.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: In other words, to spies like you, the Voice of Mundane doesn't further the Twin Empresses' interests in any way.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Junge Frau, until I saw how reckless you were, I took you for a fool.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: And now, it seems you just didn't know how to put your wits to use.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Uhh.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You're goddamned right. Here, I brought the research plan along. There's no point in hiding any of this anymore.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: The Voice of Mundane is unique. It's undoubtedly the Witch King's lingering echoes in the world, and there is definitely some power hidden within.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But the Witch King's fervent followers truly believed that the Witch King left behind his avatar within it.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: The power the Voice of Mundane holds is too unique. It will never see widespread use.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: At the very least, the current court casters see research on the Voice of Mundane as a futile and pointless pursuit.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: And that's why the handling of Ebenholz and Kreide became a problem.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Was Ebenholz chosen because he was considered safer?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Yes, we had to announce the plan's failure, and Ebenholz was naturally the best choice as there was nothing wrong with his body.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: On the contrary, as there were already problems with Kreide's body... he had no choice... Death awaited him.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But he finally got away from the Witch King's Remains! And yet he had to die... That's too cruel!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Perhaps, in your eyes, our methods are inhumane.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But once you've witnessed countless tragedies, especially ones caused by those who are not inhumane, you'll come to realize that—

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You can't let your feelings get in the way of everything.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You probably think Biegler is a pretty heartless man, don't you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Yeah, I do think so.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But what you don't know is he's lived in the Afterglow and spent time with its residents day after day for more than a dozen years. His feelings for this place is no less genuine than anyone else.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: There's no one who wants to skin Gertrude alive more than him, but he can't.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Do you think you're the angriest person to ever talk to him?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Biegler... he...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Besides, Kreide's condition endangers those around him, too. He has no way to get too close to anyone, and his past destined him to never live the life of a normal man.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: He truly didn't have a choice.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But you let your feelings get in the way with him. You offered him a choice other than death.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Is that really a choice? He had to wander the world with an old man who's half dead. He learned how to play the cello, and yet he rarely had a chance to even touch one.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: He can't make friends. He can't even get too close with anyone. Can you really call that a proper life?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But he lived.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Having seen how he trembled back then, I can still feel a sharp pain in my arms, even now.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: The Witch King... The Witch King.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I, Kreide, those who got infected inadvertently, and those who were forcefully infected...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: The wounds that the Witch King left on Leithanien have yet to heal, but now there are those who thirst for his return, and there are even nobles who are sheltering his remnants and facilitating their research.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Oh, how I dread...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I dread I won't live to see the day they all meet justice.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: *Cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You will live.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: No need to comfort me, Junge Frau.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I've lived with him for all these years. It's a miracle that I'm still alive today.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: He is like a real grandson to me.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I brought him here because I was actually thinking of introducing him to Biegler and setting him up with a job as an agent.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: That way, I would at least get to die knowing he's in good hands.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But now... It doesn't really to me so much anymore.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I always thought... it was my fate to give my life to Their Majesties as an agent, but it seems... that's not really all there is, heh...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Sir...
Crash.
A tremendous noise comes from inside.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Go, let this old grandpa sit here a little longer. Go help them.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If you don't feel well, be sure to call my name!
The Voice of Mundane did not have a name, at first.
The melody was abandoned by the Witch King, after all.
It was a melody improvised by him on the spur of the moment and transcribed by his court musicians.
If the Witch King's complete pieces are howls from a deep abyss, then these fragments are indeed still melodies of the mortal realm.
And thus, these fragments were named the Voice of Mundane.
Be that as it may, the Witch King's power is still immensely terrifying.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ebenholz, I may have asked you to show your purist form in music, but now—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I want you to think back to your life the past two dozen-or-so years. Let your resentfulness pour out.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Music is a portraiture of your life. It's the steps you take, the eyes you peer into the world with!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't let your emotions cloud you, but don't betray your emotions either! Explore, vent, and drag your melody out from the deepest parts of your soul!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I... I found it...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Right, that's it! That's exactly what I want!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That's the melody that was carved into your brain... It's the melody of destruction, and it is a ravaging one.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: And you, Kreide, I need the opposite from you. I need you to constrain yourself.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You are too unreserved. You encompass everything that you've experienced. Do you know that your kindness is your greatest weakness?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Are you reconciling? Why are you reconciling? Why should you reconcile? Who has the right to ask you to reconcile?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Everyone thinks you deserve better. The idea has crossed your mind too, hasn't it?!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You still aren't willing to change the way you think, huh?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Fine. Fine.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: This is enough.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I can feel your melody too—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: A void. A void that swallows everything whole.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hngh...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Bear with it!
The energies of two wildly different Originium Arts begin to entangle with one another inside the room as anguished expressions start to appear on the two young men's faces.
Czerny knows it is time for him to join in.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Keep playing. Do not fret. If you feel something's wrong with your body, stop immediately.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But If you do feel something's off, and you're not the one to blame——

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Then leave it to me.
Czerny sits in front of the piano, takes a deep breath, and starts playing as well.
However, when he attempts to sort out the two totally different surges of energy, he realizes just how much he overestimated his abilities.
The melody is strong, full of anger, terrifying, solemn, bloody—
Above all, it's a melody that fully immerses its listeners.
One moment, he's suddenly filled with hatred toward the Witch King. The next second, he has a heartfelt admiration for him.
One moment, he feels as though he is a newborn child, but he immediately feels the passage of time and its effects on his body. The very next second, he is as old as the hills.

He forces himself to keep his appearance intact with what little sanity he has left, but he feels as though he is walking in a boundless desert. The sandstorm is too powerful, and he cannot open his eyes.
He tries his best to shake the sand off. Then, he sees a towering wall that reaches even the sky. There is nothing on the wall. No pain, no anger, and no death.
It's a simple, unadorned wall.
At that very moment, he finally realizes. That is a wall he will never be able to overcome.
His mind is instantly filled with fear.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Gah!
Czerny coughs violently, sending blood gushing out of his mouth.
His cough is so intense that he tries to get up for a drink of water, only for him to stagger and knock down the music stand next to him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hey, are you alright?!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Herr Czerny!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I heard something just now! What happened?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: A trifle, nothing more.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Now I see it. It's not that no one has ever attempted to do what I did. It's just that people who tried are all dead.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ha, haha...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hahahahahaha!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're laughing?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, You're bleeding out of your mouth... Let me wipe that for you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: How did you two feel just now?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When we drew out the Voice of Mundane, it felt very much like I was getting torn apart.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But after you joined in, it did feel like a lot of the pressure faded.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: At the very least, this proves that my idea is workable.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But you're already...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I coughed up some blood, that's all. I know my own body better than anyone.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Let's continue.

a.text: Czerny sits back on his bench.
He closes his eyes and begins to ponder a question.
Who is Czerny?
He answers himself: Czerny is a coward.
He once hid underneath the wings of his dear friend and teacher, thinking that he could live his whole life through music.
Yet the death of his dear friend, the torments of Oripathy, and poverty all worked together to make him realize that he is but an ordinary man.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You will die.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I've lived this long because Gertrude still thinks I have value, and so she paid for my medication and kept me alive for a few years longer than most other Infected.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But if I can't finish this piece today, I might as well be dead.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you don't want me to die a meaningless death, pick up your flute.

a.text: He answers: Czerny is a man who sees music as everything.

Before he was famous, the people of the Afterglow showed nothing but grief and sorrow whenever he went outside. They had no appreciation for the beauty of music because they didn't know whether they would live to see the next day.
To make ends meet, he had no choice but to accept Gertrude's suggestion and become a spectacle for the nobles in the music halls left behind by the Witch King, like some kind of rare animal.
Life was way too complicated, and he wanted to go back inside his house.
At all those times, it was always music that kept him from running.
He has more than music, but it is with music that he expresses everything about him.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Kreide, your performance is too weak.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't worry about me. You don't have that right!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: This is about your survival, not mine. Do not ever think it is a virtue to sacrifice yourself!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Your sacrifice is also a burden!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Scream, vent, and fight for the reward that should've been yours!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I... understand.

a.text: Finally, he answers: Czerny is a man who resists fate.
Is music how he resists his fate, then?
No! Music is his struggle, his howl, and his song.
He is struggling for his friend who passed away before fulfilling her musical ideals.
He is howling for those who cannot speak.
He is singing for those who was born into suffering yet still have joy within their hearts.
In that case, is he performing in someone else's stead?
No! He knows how his friend was unwilling to die, he walked the streets where those who cannot speak gather, and he brought music to those who are trying to seek joy despite their sufferings.
Once again, he stands in front of that high wall—the Witch King. He knows he can never overcome this wall.

But, this time, he instead reminisces about the joy of discussing music with his dear friend, he remembers the love and respect he receives from the Afterglow's residents, and he remembers the morning sun he sees at the beginning of each day.
And that is why he says—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Right now, I am my own opponent.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough*, ourgh.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, you're coughing up blood again!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: (He's not listening to me at all...)

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Let's go get some rest, Ebenholz.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But––

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: We don't need to be here anymore.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: What we need to do is rest up and wait for Herr Czerny to finish his new piece.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hibiscus, take care of him.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: At the very least, I won't let him collapse before me. Now go.
Czerny's enemy is not the Witch King.
Even though the Witch King's offenses were heinously profuse, even though he disdains that monarch, he is still forced to concede that music itself stands unrelated to good or evil.
His opponent is himself, at this very moment.
He no longer tries to scale the wall so despairingly high.
He begins to perform.
Beneath his feet appears a platform. It brings him up in unbroken ascent, up through the clouds.
Though still no end to the wall can be seen, he no longer cares.
Even though he can feel the turbulent power dash about his body, and he cannot hold back further coughs of blood.
Hibiscus, to one side, is even given the illusion—
She can almost see Czerny's life flying by in accelerando, but at the same time, the score he writes rages:
Take it, take it all! Take everything of him!
Today marks the day of Czerny's death!
But Czerny's music will never die!

a.text: And day breaks.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: *cough* *cough*, *cough*, *cough*...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It's... com... plete...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's such a relief! You're—
The musician strains to lift himself, but his upper body crashes against the piano, and he leaves a discordant coda in the shining dawn.
